entries.title: Approach to Trauma: Epidemiology and Primary/Secondary Survey

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109 ('Given a patient who has sustained trauma, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and complications... and initiate an appropriate management plan') is the direct anchor for the primary/secondary survey approach that opens this chapter's trauma content.

testable_competencies.primary_survey: Perform an ABCDE primary trauma survey and identify immediately life-threatening injuries requiring intervention before secondary survey.
testable_competencies.trauma_investigations: Select appropriate initial trauma investigations (labs, FAST, CT) based on mechanism and hemodynamic status.

entries.title: Head Trauma and Mild Traumatic Brain Injury

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-10 explicitly covers diagnosis, resuscitation, imaging, and surveillance for traumatic brain injury, matching this unit's GCS-based severity stratification and mild-TBI disposition content.

testable_competencies.tbi_severity: Classify traumatic brain injury severity using GCS and determine need for CT head imaging.
testable_competencies.mtbi_disposition: Determine safe ED disposition (discharge vs. observation) for mild traumatic brain injury.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)

testable_competencies.chest_injury_recognition: Recognize and prioritize management of life-threatening chest injuries found on primary survey (tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade, flail chest, etc.).
testable_competencies.penetrating_neck_trauma: Apply a zone-based approach to penetrating neck trauma assessment and management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-1 directly covers diagnosis and management of abdominal injuries, matching this unit's blunt/penetrating abdominal trauma content.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)

testable_competencies.abdominal_trauma_mechanism: Differentiate blunt vs. penetrating abdominal trauma mechanisms and associated organ injury patterns.
testable_competencies.gu_trauma_management: Manage genitourinary tract injuries (ureteral, bladder, urethral) identified on trauma workup.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)

testable_competencies.extremity_injury_recognition: Recognize limb-threatening extremity injuries (e.g. dislocation with neurovascular compromise) requiring urgent reduction.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-12 ('Skin wounds') is the closest available presentation-level anchor for basic ED wound assessment/closure principles covered in this unit.

testable_competencies.abdo_pain_triage: Differentiate emergent (surgical/vascular) from less-emergent causes of acute abdominal pain in the ED.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 73 directly matches: identifying life-threatening causes of pelvic pain, determining pregnancy likelihood, and stabilizing hemodynamically unstable patients - exactly this unit's ED approach.

entries.title: Altered Level of Consciousness / Coma (incl. Empiric Antidotes)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)

testable_competencies.ecg_recognition: Recognize life-threatening ECG changes (STEMI-equivalents, malignant dysrhythmias).

testable_competencies.asthma_severity: Classify acute asthma severity and select appropriate escalation of therapy (bronchodilators, steroids, NIV, intubation).

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 68 (Palpitations) is the closest available MCC presentation objective for the dysrhythmia-recognition/acute-rate-or-rhythm-control competency in this unit; the objective's own scope is broader (symptom of palpitations generally) than this unit's specific arrhythmia-management algorithms.

testable_competencies.afib_acute_mgmt: Apply time-since-onset and anticoagulation criteria to guide acute AFib cardioversion decisions.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)

testable_competencies.adhf_recognition: Recognize left- and right-sided heart failure presentations and identify precipitants of acute decompensation.

entries.title: Venous Thromboembolism: DVT and Pulmonary Embolism

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)

entries.title: Electrolyte Disturbances (ED Approach)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 79-1 (Hyperkalemia) directly anchors the most emergent electrolyte disturbance covered in this unit's Table 19 (ECG changes, emergent stabilization with calcium gluconate/insulin-dextrose/kayexalate).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 99-2 (Hyponatremia) directly anchors the second emergent electrolyte disturbance covered in this unit's Table 19, including correction-rate safety (osmotic demyelination risk).

testable_competencies.electrolyte_emergency_recognition: Recognize ED-relevant electrolyte emergencies (severe hyperkalemia, hyponatremia) and initiate first-line stabilization.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Toronto Notes explicitly cross-references this content to Nephrology, NP8; Table 19 covers additional electrolytes (hypo-/hyperkalemia, hypo-/hypercalcemia, etc.) beyond the two anchored here, and full electrolyte-disturbance MCC mapping is expected to also be represented in the Nephrology chapter crosswalk - this ER unit covers only the ED-specific emergent-stabilization slice for the two objectives with confirmed dedicated MCC anchors.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 9-1 (Hypertension) directly anchors this unit's asymptomatic-severe-hypertension and hypertensive-crisis-agent content.

testable_competencies.htn_emergency_recognition: Distinguish hypertensive emergency (end-organ injury) from asymptomatic severe hypertension and select an appropriate IV agent when treatment is indicated.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: ACS is the flagship life-threatening diagnosis objective 14 (Chest pain) is designed to test for; this unit's UA/NSTEMI/STEMI classification and reperfusion-strategy content directly operationalizes that objective's management task.

testable_competencies.acs_classification: Classify ACS as UA, NSTEMI, or STEMI using biomarkers and ECG, and select reperfusion strategy (PCI vs. thrombolysis) and timing.
testable_competencies.acs_initial_mgmt: Initiate first-line ACS management (ASA, anticoagulation, antiplatelet therapy) in the ED.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Septic shock is a canonical shock subtype under objective 9-2; this unit's SIRS/sepsis/septic-shock definitional spectrum and early-recognition content operationalizes that objective.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 107-1 provides only partial supporting evidence, covering the febrile-source-identification half of sepsis workup but not shock recognition/management itself.

testable_competencies.sepsis_recognition: Apply SIRS/qSOFA criteria to recognize sepsis and septic shock and initiate early source control and resuscitation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)

entries.title: Approach to the Overdose/Poisoned Patient (History, Primary/Secondary Survey, Universal Antidotes)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 77 (Poisoning) is the direct anchor for this unit's overdose-patient history, primary/secondary survey, and universal-antidote (naloxone, etc.) content.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-13 (Spinal trauma) explicitly covers diagnosis, initial immobilization, and management of traumatic spinal cord injury, directly matching this unit's C-spine clearance criteria and spinal cord injury etiology/clinical features/investigations/treatment content.

testable_competencies.cspine_clearance: Apply clinical criteria (e.g. Canadian C-Spine Rule) to determine need for spinal immobilization and imaging after trauma.
testable_competencies.spinal_cord_injury_recognition: Recognize signs and symptoms of spinal cord injury (including spinal shock) and initiate immobilization and management.
